alt: News infographic reading 'TACHYUM FILES FOR BANKRUPTCY — Prodigy: 8 years, 1,024 cores on paper, no shipping chip' with a chip icon crossed out in orange and all promised launch years 2020 through 2025 struck through in red, ending with '2030+?' in an orange box
story: Tachyum's Prodigy processor, pitched since 2018 as a single chip beating Intel, AMD, and NVIDIA combined, missed six consecutive launch dates (2020–2025), ballooned its core-count claims from 64 to 1,024 on paper, took over $220 million in reported funding, and never publicly demonstrated working silicon before its Slovak subsidiary filed for bankruptcy on October 22, 2026.
why_funny: After eight years of raising the core count every time a launch date slipped, the only thing Tachyum actually shipped was a bankruptcy filing — Tom's Hardware had been calling it a 'meme chip' for years.
